analysis.file_name: GS Blekos - ## ECB Recap AI & Jobs Haleon Europe Indus Europe Retail Adidas Total HelleniQ ASM Neste Amazong Intel Sandisk ## 30 Oct 2026.pdf
analysis.title: European Daily: ECB Recap / AI & Jobs / Haleon / Europe Indus / Europe Retail / Adidas / Total / HelleniQ / ASM / Neste / Amazon / Intel / Sandisk
key_insights: GS maintains its forecast for one more ECB hike at the December meeting. More acute sovereign stress could lead the Council to hold, but the required tightening in financial conditions would likely need to be large given ongoing energy pressures.
GS sees an additional ECB hike in March as possible if energy prices continue to rise, but sees a significant hurdle to speeding up the pace of hikes.

Workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs take about a month longer to find new jobs and are roughly 10pp more likely to remain unemployed a year after displacement, comparable to earlier waves of technological change.

Haleon Q3 organic sales growth was 2.6%, below company-compiled consensus of +3.2%. Guidance was cut on two previously uncommunicated items: a halt of Centrum OTC imports into China (c.£75m FY25 sales, c.70bps full-year headwind) and a LatAm route-to-market change (£15-20m Q4 sales headwind). GS cuts EPS by 3%.
Haleon organic growth by region: Asia Pacific +3.9%, Europe -0.6%. Oral Health grew +8.8% and was 38% of group sales in 9M.
Europe multi-industry heatmap: the picture is broadly stable across regions. Sequential improvement is concentrated in data center/semis, while marine, rail and autos have deteriorated.
GS changed estimates and price targets for ABB, Atlas Copco, Konecranes, Nexans, Schindler, Signify and SKF. 2027 orders/sales/adj. EBIT move by 1%/1%/1% on average.
UK HAC: GS sees minimal near-term budget impact, and updates 2027E HAC growth to +1.4% (from +1.9%) and 2026E to +3.5% (from +2.1%).

Adidas 3Q26: apparel grew +19% cFX y/y with originals apparel +45%. Running +19%, Football +13%, Training +17%. Footwear was flat overall as excess US and Europe wholesale inventory weighs on lifestyle footwear, which management says may strengthen in 2H27. TP unchanged at €180, Neutral.

TotalEnergies 3Q26 adjusted net income was US$9.1bn, 2% above company-compiled consensus of US$8.9bn. OCF (pre-OWC) was US$12.3bn, 1% above consensus of US$12.1bn. Strong refining and gas trading drove c.US$6bn net debt reduction and buybacks step up to US$2.5bn per quarter. GS stays Neutral.

GS downgrades HelleniQ Energy to Neutral from Buy with the €20.0 PT unchanged. At €18.71 the PT implies 7% upside vs a 30% average for Buy-rated EU Energy names. The company has c.50% middle distillates exposure and strong FCF.

ASM International 3Q26 call: Advanced Logic/Foundry is expected to be the key 2027 growth driver, memory demand is supported by HBM capacity additions with limited impact from possible delays in the move to 4F2, gross margin is constructive despite component-cost inflation, and China demand remains robust though the MATCH Act implications are unclear.

Neste 3Q26 comparable EBITDA was €1,555mn, 29% above Vara consensus of €1,202mn. Renewable Products EBITDA was €1,011mn (20% above consensus) and Oil Products EBITDA was €504mn (48% above consensus). Rated Buy.
Amazon Q3'26 review: GS sees management's framing of AWS revenue growth and operating margin trajectory as key to long-term fundamentals, and sees compelling risk/reward from current levels.
Intel: servers very strong, but PC weakness is likely a setback for the stock.
SanDisk: tight supply/demand conditions drive estimates as datacenter exposure moves higher.

Adidas 3Q26 apparel momentum is offset by flat footwear from lifestyle inventory issues. Investors likely cautious until footwear inflects.
TotalEnergies 3Q26 adjusted net income beat consensus by 2%. Neutral on relative valuation.
Neste comparable EBITDA was 29% above consensus, with record Renewable Products volumes.
GS sees compelling risk/reward from current levels after Q3'26, with AWS growth and margin trajectory the key narratives.
Servers are very strong, but PC weakness is likely a setback for the stock.
Tight supply/demand conditions drive estimates as datacenter exposure moves higher.
Haleon EPS cut by 3% after the guidance cut on China and LatAm headwinds.

sector_views.rationale: Broadly stable picture across regions. Sequential improvement is concentrated in DC/semis, while marine, rail and autos have deteriorated.
HelleniQ moved to Neutral after a re-rating, and TotalEnergies stays Neutral. Refining and middle distillate markets remain tight.
Haleon cut guidance on China and LatAm headwinds, partly offset by Oral Health strength.
